standard.title: Perform to audiences with intention
standard.description: perform improvised, devised and/or scripted drama to audiences, using performance skills and conventions to shape the drama
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can rehearse and perform drama to audiences using performance skills and conventions relevant to style and form (Y7-8). They can collect and evaluate audience feedback and reflect on how respectful relationships and empathy were applied and interpreted.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students perform improvised, devised and/or scripted drama to audiences, using performance skills and conventions to shape the drama.

nodes.label: Performing with sustained intentionality
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can sustain a coherent performance throughout — maintaining intentional character, vocal delivery and physical presence in alignment with unified dramatic meaning.
nodes.minimum_width: Student sustains performance — character, voice, physicality — across a full scene or piece with consistent intentionality.
nodes.typical_width: Students convey tensions in stories, characters, relationships and dialogue through voice, movement and symbol; they engage audiences and elicit responses; they sustain presentation in a class or stage context; they adhere to protocols when performing material connected to community ownership.
wider: Students perform in a sustained, extended context (multi-scene work, community presentation, festival showing) where stamina and consistency across a longer arc is required
Students perform devised drama created in a shared process with community members, observing protocols for collective ownership and cultural authority
nodes.hinge_reason: Sustained intentionality — performance in alignment with a unified intention across the whole work — is what distinguishes Y9-10 performance from earlier bands; without it, students can produce technically competent moments that don't cohere into a purposeful whole.

response_modes.reason: Sustained performance coherence develops through run-through rehearsals of the whole work, not just scene-by-scene work; students need experience of performing through, not just in, a drama.

success_criteria: Student sustains performance intention — character, voice, physicality — across a complete scene or piece
Student's performance is consistent with the drama's unified meaning (does not have isolated technically good moments that contradict the whole)

nodes.label: Evaluating performance and drawing forward
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate how successfully their performance achieved its intentions and draw specific lessons for future dramatic practice.
nodes.minimum_width: Student produces a performance evaluation that addresses at least three dimensions (intention, execution, audience effect) and draws at least one lesson for future practice.
nodes.typical_width: Students reflect on and evaluate how successfully intentions, meaning and effects were achieved in context; they consider use of elements, conventions, performance skills and design; they identify what can be learnt from this for future dramatic practice.
wider: Students compare their own evaluation of the performance with collected audience feedback, analysing the gap between intended and experienced meaning
Students use a structured performance review framework consistently across multiple performances, tracking their development across the year

response_modes.reason: Post-performance evaluation is the culminating integration of performance skills, reflective practice and dramatic intention; it closes the make-perform-reflect cycle and generates the foundation for continued development.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Performing across multiple contexts — different drama forms, different audiences, community collaboration — generates richer evaluation material and deeper learning about the relationship between intention and audience experience.
success_criteria: Student evaluates their performance across at least three dimensions: intention, execution, audience effect
Student draws at least one specific lesson for future practice
Student demonstrates appropriate cultural protocols when performing material connected to community ownership or cultural knowledge
